verificationHighlights.realProcessing: Actual PCM WAV fixtures encoded by FFmpeg to MP3, probed, fully decoded for duration and SHA-256 checked through authenticated HTTP. Original WAV bytes unchanged; duplicate/concurrent deliveries commit one output.
verificationHighlights.durability: Real outbox/BullMQ dispatch, queue obliteration after SQL dispatch acknowledgement, reconstructed dispatch, actual closed producer connection and reconnect; SQL intent remains authoritative.
verificationHighlights.nodeCrashRecovery: Production handler forked as a real Node process on both PostgreSQL and persistent SQLite, SIGKILL during partial output, after verified output/before commit, and after commit/before handler acknowledgement. Restart retains one ready reference and two files; attempts=2 before commit, attempts=1 after commit.
verificationHighlights.faultInjectionDisclosure: Persisted lease/output deadlines are moved into the past after the worker is killed to accelerate takeover; cooldown timestamps are backdated to exercise lost-Redis replay. These are explicit fault injections, not sleeps or weakened readiness assertions.
verificationHighlights.retirementAndOwnership: Replace/delete/archive/suspend during actual processing never commit stale output; current-owner/role/head/source revisions checked. Late old fences cannot commit/delete newer results. Chapter edits require explicit retry.
verificationHighlights.failureAndLimits: Corrupted source, invalid generated output, missing FFmpeg dependency, output cap, quota denial, four-attempt exhaustion, bounded subprocess timeout and orphan cleanup exercised. Missing/corrupt ready derivative requires actual server-side integrity failure before explicit repair.
verificationHighlights.migrations: Fresh PostgreSQL/SQLite and populated upgrade backfill preserve source/favorites and atomically create pending intent/outbox; backfilled work is immediately due. Existing schema simulation fixtures retain preservation assertions.
verificationHighlights.importAndBackup: Actual processed source imported SQLite→PostgreSQL with metadata retained, unavailable outputs retired/uncharged, intent failed and no stale dispatch; existing target result wins. Real populated 28-table PostgreSQL backup/restore fingerprints include intent, output and typed outbox data. Files are outside the database archive.
verificationHighlights.operations: Checksum verification CLI checks original and ready output; existing upload restart check still verifies source-only operation.
verificationHighlights.browser: Both databases show real pending/claimed/ready state, native MP3 playback, original WAV, actual missing-file error/controlled rebuild, refresh and private no-caching under an actively controlling PWA; mobile/logout behavior checked.
verificationHighlights.docker: Current API/worker images built. Genuine upload pending before worker exists; actual 1 CPU/512 MiB worker dispatches/encodes. Worker SIGKILL + volatile Redis restart recover SQL work; API restart preserves WAV/MP3 references/range bytes on a new private volume. Anonymous/public reads denied. Only new test containers/network/volume removed.
verificationHighlights.buildAndFormat: Clean-export and workspace production builds passed; formatting, changed docs/Compose formatting and git diff --check passed.

schema.outboxExtension: background_jobs.dispatch_topic=private_audio typed maintenance envelope; no destructive rebuild of the constrained job table
schema.sourceOwnershipBinding: Composite FK against private asset/user/story/chapter; unique ready output per intent

contract.identity: private-audio:{assetUUID}:{sha256}:processor-v1 in SQL; SHA-256(identity:generation) BullMQ ID avoids forbidden colons
contract.states: pending, processing (hashing/transcoding/validating), ready, failed, superseded; output writing/ready/orphan/deleted
contract.retries: Four encoding attempts/generation, 1/2/4-second exponential backoff (60-second cap), explicit revision-guarded retry/repair, ten generations and forty attempts maximum
contract.lease: Three subprocess timeouts + 45 seconds; no SQL transaction held during FFmpeg; current exact fence/eligibility required at commit
contract.retention: Immutable per-attempt keys registered before creation; source and unreleased derivative reservations share creator quota. Deletion only frees quota after confirmed unlink, and never targets another attempt/current source key.
contract.sourceIdentity: Full source hash plus hash/count of bytes actually fed into FFmpeg; complete generated-file SHA-256 and decode validation
contract.format: Private MP3, libmp3lame 96 kb/s stereo 44100 Hz; ready is technical readiness, never publication authority

issuesFoundAndFixed: Crash test initially exited before its partial-output checkpoint because the optional output hook was not forwarded; wiring the real stream checkpoint now proves bytes exist before SIGKILL on both databases.
Browser media buffers masked a deleted file. A fresh media element after reload and an explicit 503 HEAD check now exercise actual storage failure and guarded rebuild, without arbitrary sleeps.
The Docker API ephemeral host port changed across restart. The drill follows docker port after restart rather than polling a stale address.

PostgreSQL backfill timestamps could defer immediately eligible work relative to the worker clock. Backfilled intent/outbox availability is now explicitly already due, while creation timestamps remain audited.
Source hashing now covers the exact stream fed into FFmpeg as well as admission, and process-exit guards prevent late RSS callbacks signalling a completed subprocess group.
Typed outbox ownership, missing binary classification, original/attempt cleanup lease protection and missing-outbox recreation are explicit; no broker-only readiness or fake progress is used.
infrastructureIncident: A final Docker rebuild timed out and then hit a containerd snapshot input/output error; host storage headroom was low. A normal non-destructive Colima stop/start restored image-store reads. The complete final Docker drill subsequently passed all six checks. No global prune, filesystem repair or developer-volume recreation was performed.
limitations: Private local-volume storage only; S3/multi-host filesystem behavior, public deployment and remote GitHub Actions remain unverified.

macOS uses sampled RSS monitoring rather than an instantaneous hard OS ceiling. Linux uses process CPU/address-space limits plus the tested Docker 1 CPU/512 MiB cgroup. Actual RAM-OOM/power-loss/kernel-I/O-hang fault injection was not performed.

Only small genuine PCM fixtures (including partial-output crash work) and local Chrome were tested. No new throughput/capacity benchmarks, cross-browser or production-scale/security certification claim.

Database and source/derivative volume backups must match; no atomic live DB/filesystem snapshot or full remote disaster-recovery drill. Database-only import deliberately invalidates unavailable bytes.
Per-creator quotas do not provide a global disk budget. Retained asset/attempt metadata is bounded but operational disk/backlog monitoring and long-term retention policy remain follow-up work.

Synchronized host clocks are required for timely leases/deadlines; token fencing rejects stale commits after takeover. Exact-once execution and byte-identical MP3 across encoder versions are not claimed.
No public publishing, licensing attestation, moderation, signed/public CDN media, additional input formats, WebSockets or creator analytics were introduced.
Optional unrelated SMTP/supervisor/load checks were not rerun. New resource-intensive private Docker drill was run locally and remains optional CI tooling.
